title: Lift a fixed-prior binary classical SDPI to arbitrary finite quantum references
statement: For a finite-output binary-input channel T and full-support fixed prior pi, the fixed-prior scalar Umegaki SDPI coefficient eta(T,pi) also bounds arbitrary positive operator weights A0,A1 on any finite quantum reference through the displayed inequality; scalar weights attain the same coefficient.

requires: Finite-output binary-input channel T, full-support fixed prior pi, A0,A1 positive semidefinite on one finite-dimensional space, K=A0+A1, and q_y=(Tpi)_y.
provides: Exact equality of the scalar fixed-prior Umegaki SDPI coefficient and its version with arbitrary finite quantum reference dimension.
assumptions: Use Y_y=T_y0 A0+T_y1 A1, omit q_y=0 outputs, and take D as Umegaki relative entropy for positive operators of arbitrary trace; support is automatic from A_i<=K and pi_i>0.
costs: Algebraic lifting of a scalar inequality using the two-source entropy identity; no experimental access, sample bound, or algorithmic cost is provided.
contract.units: Umegaki relative entropy in nats; coefficients eta, T and pi are dimensionless.
contract.obstruction: The result fixes a binary transmitted alphabet and one prior. It does not establish a general multi-symbol quantum-reference theorem or a fixed-prior matrix-SDPI separation.

body: Let q_y=(Tpi)_y, K=A0+A1 and Y_y=T_y0A0+T_y1A1. Expand each divergence relative to q_yK or pi_iK into -S of its first argument, the linear trace terms from log q_y/log pi_i, and a reference term involving Tr K log K. Since sum_yY_y=K and sum_iA_i=K, the common reference term cancels in the output-minus-eta-input comparison. The remaining entropy terms are -sum_y S(Y_y)+eta sum_i S(A_i)+(1-eta)S(K), with Y_y and K nonnegative mixtures of A0,A1. For each source coefficient, -sum_y T_yi+eta+(1-eta)=0, so both balance equations hold. The rest is linear in Tr A0,Tr A1. The scalar fixed-prior SDPI inequality therefore lifts by U993. Scalar references give the reverse coefficient inequality. Rows with q_y=0 have T_y0=T_y1=0 because pi has full support and are omitted.
